extracted.intended_audience: recipients of federal financial assistance (schools, colleges, universities), Title IX coordinators, campus administrators, and institutional legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements for how recipients must define, investigate, respond to, document, and adjudicate reports of sexual harassment under the Department's Title IX regulations and preamble guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of complainant and respondent
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'complainant' is any individual who has been alleged to be the victim of conduct that could constitute sexual harassment, and a 'respondent' is any individual who has been reported to be the perpetrator of conduct that could constitute sexual harassment; a person may be a complainant or respondent regardless of whether a formal complaint has been filed or a grievance is pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §106.30 definitions; this status depends on allegation/reporting, not on filing a formal complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal complaint definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'formal complaint' is defined as a document filed by a complainant or signed by a Title IX Coordinator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §106.30; formal complaint status triggers specific grievance-process obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anyone may report
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may report sexual harassment to a recipient regardless of whether the reporter is the alleged victim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §106.8(a); reporting is not limited to the alleged victim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures: availability and notice in grievance process
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's grievance process must describe the range of supportive measures available to complainants and respondents, and the Title IX Coordinator must contact an individual complainant to discuss the availability of supportive measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §106.45(b)(1)(ix) and §106.44(a); grievance procedures should explicitly enumerate supportive measures and ensure coordinators proactively discuss them with complainants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures: recordkeeping and rationale for not providing
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must create and maintain for seven years records of any actions, including any supportive measures, taken in response to a report or formal complaint and must document the basis for concluding the response was not deliberately indifferent; if supportive measures are not provided, the recipient must document why that decision was not clearly unreasonable given the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §106.45(b)(10)(ii); documentation must show rationale to demonstrate non-deliberate indifference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency removal and administrative leave
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations permit emergency removal of a respondent who poses an immediate threat to any person's physical health or safety, and permit placement of non-student employees on administrative leave during a pending grievance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §106.44(c) (emergency removal) and §106.44(d) (administrative leave for employees); removals must comply with regulation-specific procedural safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education program or activity: substantial control test
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of §106.44, §106.30, and §106.45, 'education program or activity' includes locations, events, or circumstances over which the recipient exercised substantial control over both the respondent and the context in which the harassment occurs, and includes buildings owned or controlled by a student organization officially recognized by a postsecondary institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See revised §106.44(a); recipients must assess whether they exercised substantial control over the context and harasser (even for some off-campus incidents) to determine Title IX coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory dismissal limited to Title IX scope; alternative conduct processes may apply
rubrics_metrics.description: A mandatory dismissal because alleged conduct did not occur in the recipient's education program or activity is a dismissal for Title IX purposes only and does not preclude the recipient from addressing the conduct under other provisions of its code of conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §106.45(b)(3) and related preamble discussion; recipients should consider alternative disciplinary or conduct rules even when Title IX dismissal is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals on mandatory dismissal determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Complainants and respondents equally may appeal a recipient's determination that allegations were subject to mandatory dismissal under §106.45(b)(3)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §106.45(b)(8); appeal rights apply to dismissal determinations as specified in the regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Attempting to participate" includes applicants and re-enrollees
rubrics_metrics.description: A complainant may be 'attempting to participate' in the recipient's education program or activity where the complainant has applied for admission, or where the complainant has withdrawn but indicates a desire to re-enroll if the recipient appropriately responds to sexual harassment allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See preamble discussion; Title IX protections can attach to those seeking to participate, not only current enrolled students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliberate indifference and liability threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's liability (and the concept of deliberate indifference) requires, at minimum, that an official with authority to address the alleged discrimination has actual knowledge of discrimination in the recipient's programs and fails to respond adequately; deliberate indifference must cause students to undergo harassment or make them vulnerable to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preamble relies on Gebser and Davis: actual knowledge by an appropriate official and failure to act are central; recipients must provide prompt, effective responses to avoid liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot rely on restricting constitutional rights to show non-deliberate indifference
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department may not deem a recipient to have satisfied its duty to not be deliberately indifferent based on the recipient's restriction of rights protected under the U.S. Constitution (e.g., First, Fifth, Fourteenth Amendments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §106.6(d) and §106.44(a); recipients must respect constitutional protections while responding and cannot justify inaction by invoking restriction of protected rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations under other federal laws (disability laws) remain
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in these final regulations affects a recipient's obligations to comply with all applicable disability laws (such as the ADA); if sexual-harassment-related conduct causes or exacerbates a disability, recipients must comply with disability-law requirements (including reasonable accommodations) irrespective of whether the sexual harassment constitutes Title IX sexual harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See preamble discussion and Directed Question 5; recipients must handle disability accommodations separately from Title IX determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of off-campus conduct effects in hostile-environment analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Schools should consider the effects of off-campus conduct when evaluating whether there is a hostile environment on campus — for example, earlier off-campus sexual assault followed by on-campus taunting should be taken into account and may require protective steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites 2011 Dear Colleague Letter and case examples; even if initial conduct occurred off-campus, subsequent on-campus effects can make a hostile environment under Title IX and require action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between Title IX program/activity coverage and Clery Act geography
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX's concept of 'education program or activity' and Clery Act 'geography' serve different purposes and are defined differently; buildings owned/controlled by recognized student organizations may be included in Title IX program/activity analysis even where Clery geography differs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See references to 20 U.S.C. 1092(f)(6)(iii), Clery Act regulations, and preamble discussion; recipients should treat Title IX and Clery obligations separately when assessing coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Records and retention (supportive measures and response documentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must retain records of actions taken in response to reports/formal complaints, including supportive measures and documentation supporting conclusions regarding deliberate indifference, for a period of seven years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §106.45(b)(10)(ii); maintain retrievable documentation to demonstrate compliance and rationale for responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative interpretation parity with judicial standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department intends to apply the same statutory-text analysis to administrative enforcement (by the Department) as courts do in judicial enforcement when interpreting 'program or activity' and related Title IX statutory language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preamble states consistency with Davis Court approach; recipients should expect administrative application consistent with statutory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdictional limitation: 'against a person in the U.S.'
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 106.44(a) includes discussion of the jurisdictional limitation that Title IX protects any person 'in the United States' and other jurisdictional limits on the statute's scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must consider both the location of the parties and the context/control factors when determining whether Title IX applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX objectives (policy purpose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX's objectives are two-fold: to avoid the use of Federal resources to support discriminatory practices, and to provide individual citizens effective protection against those practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Cannon v. Univ. of Chicago; recipients should interpret obligations in light of these dual aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Off-campus incidents may be Title IX-covered if facts show substantial control
rubrics_metrics.description: Even incidents occurring off campus (e.g., in off-campus apartments or social settings) may be part of a recipient's education program or activity if the recipient exercised substantial control over the context and the alleged harasser.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preamble gives examples and case law (e.g., Lapka) illustrating when off-campus conduct grew out of on-duty/training contexts; determinations are fact-specific.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient may address conduct outside Title IX via other codes
rubrics_metrics.description: If conduct is outside Title IX coverage (mandatory dismissal), the recipient is still permitted — and in some cases expected — to address the conduct through other codes of conduct or institutional disciplinary mechanisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See preamble response to commenters; mandatory Title IX dismissal is not a bar to institutional action under other authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance process scope: dismissal and related procedural cross-references
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections §106.44(a) and §106.45(b)(1)(i),(vi),(ix) and §106.45(b)(3) set out cross-referenced procedural obligations (e.g., scope, supportive measures, dismissal rules) that recipients must incorporate into grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should ensure their grievance procedures reflect the interrelated regulatory provisions cited in the preamble and include explicit cross-references as required.
